title: Incomplete Library Class / Framework Subclassing
pattern: An application struct implements a massive third-party framework trait directly to inject minor custom behaviors, coupling the domain struct to the entire framework signature.
why_bad: It exposes the application to "Framework Captivity." The application structure is constrained by the framework's design decisions. If the framework updates its trait signature, the application's core code breaks.
detection: A domain struct directly implementing large, non-local traits that contain many unrelated lifecycle or utility methods.
counterexample: Implementing highly cohesive, single-method standard traits (e.g., `Default`, `Clone`, `AsRef`) which represent fundamental compile-time concepts.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Incomplete Library Class"); Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Chapter 2 ("Inheritance").
